'''''Nymphaea rubra''''' is a species of waterlily native to the region spanning from [[Sri Lanka]] and northeastern [[India]] to western and central [[Malesia]]. Additionally, it has been introduced to regions such as Southeast China, Cuba, Guyana, Hungary, and Suriname.<ref name = "POWO, 2024">{{cite POWO |id=605694-1 |title=''Nymphaea rubra'' Roxb. ex Andrews |accessdate=4 January 2024}}</ref>

===Vegetative characteristics===
''Nymphaea rubra'' has 15.1 cm long, and 7.9 cm wide [[Rhizome|rhizomes]].<ref name = "Hossain et al., 2007" /> The [[Petiole (botany)|petiolate]], [[Orbicular (botany)|orbicular]] leaves are 25–48 cm wide. The adaxial leaf surface is bronzy red to dark green, and the abaxial leaf surface is dark purple. The leaf venation is very prominent.<ref name = "Guruge et al., 2016">{{Citation|last1=Guruge|first1=D. S. K.|last2= Yakandawala|first2=D.|last3= Yakandawala|first3=K|year=2016|url=http://aquaria.palo-alto.ca.us/plants/n/Nymphaea/rubra/Confirming_the_identity_of_newly_recorded_Nymphaea.pdf |title=Confirming the identity of newly recorded ''Nymphaea rubra'' Roxb. ex Andrews discerning from ''Nymphaea pubescens'' Willd. using morphometrics and molecular sequence analyses.|journal=Bangladesh Journal of Plant Taxonomy|volume=23|issue=2}}</ref> The petiole is 140 cm long.<ref name = "Hossain et al., 2007" />

===Generative characteristics===
The flowers are 15–25 cm wide.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The four purplish-red [[Sepal|sepals]] are oblong to lanceolate.<ref name = "La‐ongsri et al., 2009">{{Citation
|last1=La-ongsri
|first1=W.
|last2=Trisonthi
|first2=C.
|last3=Balslev
|first3=H
|year=2009
|url=https://www.academia.edu/download/53868440/j.1756-1051.2009.00295.x20170715-15689-lsccl3.pdf
|title=A synopsis of Thai Nymphaeaceae
|journal=Nordic Journal of Botany
|volume=27
|issue=2|pages=97–114}}</ref> The 12–20 narrowly oval petals have a rounded apex. The [[Stamen|androecium]] consists of 55 red stamens.<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /> The [[gynoecium]] consists of 16–21 carpels.<ref name = "La‐ongsri et al., 2009" /> The fruit bears 1.85 mm long, and 1.6 mm wide seeds.<ref name = "Conard, 1905">Conard, H. S. (2015). The Waterlilies: A Monograph of the Genus ''Nymphaea'' (Classic Reprint). pp. 199–200. USA: FB&C Limited.</ref> The peduncle is 116 cm long.<ref name = "Hossain et al., 2007" />
The flowers are pleasantly fragrant.<ref name="Henkel et al., 1907">{{Citation|last1=Henkel|first1=F.|last2=Rehnelt|first2=F.|last3=Dittmann|first3=L.
|year=1907|url=https://archive.org/details/Henkel_Nymphaeaceen/page/n73/mode/1up|title=Das Buch der Nymphaeaceen oder Seerosengewächse|page=72}}</ref>

The [[Ploidy|diploid]] [[chromosome]] count is 2n = 56.<ref name = "Hossain et al., 2007">{{Cite journal|last1=Hossain|first1=A.|last2=Kabir|first2=G.|last3=Ud-deen|first3=M. M.|last4=Alam|first4=A. M. S.|year=2007|url=https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?repid=rep1&type=pdf&doi=8dae6487226a6e4fa9ae66c759bb89878b6c77c7|title=Cytological studies of ''Nymphaea'' species available in Bangladesh|journal=Journal of Bio-Science|pages=7–13|issn=1023-8654}}.</ref>

==Reproduction==
===Vegetative reproduction===
One case of the development of a proliferating [[Pseudanthium|pseudanthia]] has been reported for a ''Nymphaea rubra'' specimen cultivated in the [[Botanical Garden of the University of Heidelberg]], Germany in 1886.<ref name = "Bleisch, 1886">Franz Bleisch. (1886). [https://books.google.com/books?id=9ORIAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22Nymphaea%20rubra%22&pg=PA326 "Abnorme Blüte von ''Nymphaea rubra''."] Deutsches Magazin Für Garten- Und Blumenkunde, 39, 326.</ref> It is [[stoloniferous]], but in rare cases it can also reproduce through proliferating pseudanthia.<ref name = "Mitra, 1990">Mitra RL (1990) Nymphaeaceae. In: Nayar MP, Thothathri K, Sanjappa M (eds) [https://bsi.gov.in/uploads/documents/Public_Information/publication/books/fascicles_of_flora_of_India_latest/Fascicle%2020.pdf Fascicles of flora of India, Fascicles 20.] Botanical Survey of India, Kolkata, pp. 20–21.</ref>

===Generative reproduction===
''Nymphaea rubra'' may reproduce [[apomictic]]ally.<ref name = "Wiersema, 1988">Wiersema, J. H. (1988). Reproductive Biology of ''Nymphaea'' (Nymphaeaceae). Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden, 75(3), 795–804. https://doi.org/10.2307/2399367</ref><ref name = "Mitra, 1990" />

==Taxonomy==
===Publication===
It was first named by [[William Roxburgh]], but only later validly published by [[Henry Cranke Andrews]] in 1808.<ref name = "POWO, 2024" /> Its status is uncertain and it may be of hybrid origin.<ref name = "Löhne et al., 2008" />

===Placement within ''Nymphaea''===
It is placed in [[Nymphaea subg. Lotos|''Nymphaea'' subg. ''Lotos'']].<ref name = "Conard, 1905" /><ref name = "Löhne et al., 2008">Löhne, C., Yoo, M. J., Borsch, T., Wiersema, J., Wilde, V., Bell, C. D., ... & Soltis, P. S. (2008). [https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/tax.574008 Biogeography of Nymphaeales: extant patterns and historical events.] Taxon, 57(4), 1123-19E.</ref>

==Etymology==
The specific epithet ''rubra'' means "red".<ref name = "Joe et al., 2016">{{cite journal|last1=Joe|first1= A.|last2= Sreejith|first2=P. E.|last3=Sabu|first3=M.|year=2016|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298791694|title=Notes on ''Musa rubra'' Kurz (Musaceae) and reduction of ''M. laterita'' Cheesman as conspecific.|journal=Taiwania|volume=61|issue=1|pages=34–40}}</ref><ref name = "Dictionary of Botanical Epithets">Dictionary of Botanical Epithets. (n.d.-b). Retrieved January 4, 2024, from https://botanicalepithets.net/dictionary/dictionary.159.html</ref>

==Ecology==
[[File:Water lily (Nymphaea rubra) Pond near Karikalampakkam, Pondy IMG 4271.JPG|thumb|right|Numerous ''Nymphaea rubra'' flowering in a pond in Karikalampakkam, India]]

===Habitat===
It occurs in rivers, lakes, and ponds.<ref name = "India Biodiversity Portal">''Nymphaea rubra'' Roxb. ex Salisb. (n.d.). India Biodiversity Portal. Retrieved January 4, 2024, from https://indiabiodiversity.org/species/show/230505</ref>

==Use==
The peduncles, and seeds are used as food.<ref name = "Juffe Bignoli, 2011" />

==Cultivation==
It is suitable for the cultivation in aquaria.<ref name = "Flowgrow">''Nymphaea rubra'' - Rote Seerose. (n.d.). Flowgrow. Retrieved January 4, 2024, from https://www.flowgrow.de/db/wasserpflanzen/nymphaea-rubra</ref><ref name = "Juffe Bignoli, 2011" />
